text: 'Avengers: Endgame' is a well executed story that centers its characters and their journeys, while providing some of the best action sequences the MCU has ever had.

It moves quickly and avoids the bloated running time that has plagued many of these films, it has some nice bits of humor sprinkled throughout and, most importantly, the strong and entertaining Brie Larson performance.
The film constantly manages to subvert expectations, while remaining firmly within the action-packed superhero genre.
It is this part of the story, the human side, to narrow it down to our marginal planet, that holds the movie together for its three-hour run time.

Dune is sci-fi world building at its best. Great visuals and design, punishing Hans Zimmer score, charismatic cast. Stellan Skarsgard steals the show as the s-f villain to top all villains. Goodbye Emperor Ming.
The Star Wars film we needed (a palate cleanser). Funny, full of action and lots of feels, this new entry achieves great balance between nostalgia and novelty. [Full review in Spanish]
An eye-popping, insult to the intelligence strictly for the kiddies and crackpot doomsday enthusiasts.
Arrival never fully escapes from the bounds of its source material.
To the 60-plus-hours of theatrical content that have so far rolled off the Disney/Marvel assembly line, this fourth Thor-centric caper adds a mostly painless if largely pointless 120 minutes.
Just put a bucket of generic Batman in here and stir in a few pints of own-label Superman. That will do to be going on with.
Although there are few worthwhile scenes, the sequel is pretty much a missed opportunity.
Black Widow is not as tedious and self-serious an entry as some of them. But that is setting the bar low.
